The "The Great Gatsby" is a classic American novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald, published in 1925. It is set in the Roaring Twenties and explores themes of wealth, class, and the American Dream.

Key Characters:

  • Jay Gatsby: A mysterious millionaire who throws lavish parties in hopes of reuniting with his former love, Daisy Buchanan.
  • Nick Carraway: The narrator of the story, who becomes Gatsby's neighbor and friend.
  • Daisy Buchanan: A wealthy socialite and the object of Gatsby's obsession.
  • Tom Buchanan: Daisy's wealthy and arrogant husband.

Major Themes:

  • The American Dream: The novel critiques the idea that anyone can achieve success through hard work, showing how wealth can lead to moral decay.
  • Class and Social Status: The distinction between "old money" (the Buchanans) and "new money" (Gatsby) is a central conflict.
  • Love and Obsession: Gatsby's intense, almost delusional devotion to Daisy drives much of the plot.

Symbolism:

  • The Green Light: Represents Gatsby's hopes and dreams for the future.
  • The Valley of Ashes: Symbolizes the moral and social decay caused by uninhibited pursuit of wealth.
  • The Eyes of Doctor T.J. Eckleburg: Represent the eyes of God watching over a spiritually empty society.
